newsitem.title: CROATIA: Viktor Lenac signs on full share listing in Zagreb.
newsitem.headline: Viktor Lenac signs on full share listing in Zagreb.

text.p: Ship repair company Viktor Lenac is to list its shares on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, saying it would help its image. Trading starts on Tuesday.
The company will list 1.06 million shares and become the fourth Croatian company to meet the exchange's listing criteria.

Viktor Lenac Director Damir Vrhovnik told Reuters, after signing the listing agreement with the exchange on Monday, "We have been working on this for some ten years which is the period that the transition of Viktor Lenac has lasted. The actual preparations for the full listing on the Zagreb stock exchange lasted some six months."
The 100-year-old company repairs and refurbishes vessels and builds platforms for off-shore installations.

"For the time being we have no plans to get listed on foreign stock exchanges, although it is hard to say what will happen. If there is some major increase in capital, then this remains a possibility," Vrhovnik said.

The company is 100 percent privatised and some 66 percent of the shares are in the hands of foreign investors, Vrhovnik said. "We are mainly export-oriented and we work for all the flags of the maritime world," he added.
Viktor Lenac will be the fifth fully-listed issue on Croatia's central bourse alongside drugs firm Pliva, Zagrebacka Banka ordinaries and the ordinary and preferred shares of Varazdinska Banka.

Marinko Papuga, director of the Zagreb Stock Exchange, said before signing the agreement, "Viktor Lenac is the first company that was not pressed to get a bourse listing by foreign investors. It is the first company to be listed that has its basic activities close to the sea, and this may result in more shippers becoming listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange."
The company said on Friday it had increased its capital to 106.2 million kuna and split its stock ahead of its listing.
The share price was rounded up to 400 kuna after being converted from the 100 German mark face value, a secretary of the board told Reuters by telephone. The new nominal share price is 100 kuna.
